summary: Every-5-minute cron that launches a new browser for each of 12 pages with a 10-minute keep_alive and never closes it.

expected_findings.explanation: captureAll() launches one browser per page and never calls browser.close(), so each session stays open until its inactivity timeout, which keep_alive sets to 10 minutes. 12 launches every 5 minutes, each billed about 10 minutes, is about 2 browser hours per run and about 576 hours a day: roughly 17,000 browser hours a month against 10 included, about $1,550 a month at $0.09 an hour, plus about 24 concurrent browsers against 10 included. The rate is fixed (12 pages on a fixed schedule), so it is a repeating path at a fixed rate, far above about $100 a month: High, with no users.

may_flag.reason: Each run stores 12 new screenshots under a new key and nothing deletes them, so the bucket grows by about 100,000 objects a month. The writes stay inside the Class A allowance; the growth is a smaller, separate problem.
